verdict.rationale: LangGraph's first-party docs describe interrupts that pause graph execution at specific points to wait for external input. Execution resumes by re-invoking the graph with Command, whose value becomes the return value of interrupt() inside the node. Checkpointers persist the paused state, and the docs name human-in-the-loop as a supported use, which community comments on human-in-the-loop with time travel corroborate. Missing for 10: no hands-on or independent walkthrough of an approval/resume cycle specifically (community corroboration is general, not a tested pause-approve-resume run).

support.subject: As a developer, I can pause an agent mid-run for human input or approval and resume with the human's decision

citations.quote: Interrupts allow you to pause graph execution at specific points and wait for external input before continuing.
you resume execution by re-invoking the graph using Command, which then becomes the return value of the interrupt() call from inside the node
Checkpointing keeps your place: the checkpointer writes the exact graph state so you can resume later, even when in an error state.
Human-in-the-loop — Seamlessly incorporate human oversight by inspecting and modifying agent state at any point during execution.
